title: Designing Backup Redundancy People Will Maintain
summary: Quarterly off-host backups and preserved launch states extended recovery beyond a one-month hosting window.
principles: Simple and maintained beats comprehensive and abandoned.
looking_back: The ‘Most Recent Backup’ folder intentionally sacrifices historical accumulation for immediate clarity. It supplements rolling hosting backups rather than attempting to replace every recovery layer.
body: Hosting retained only one month of rolling backups, and original launch-state files were not being preserved.
The process needed to supplement hosting, remain easy to perform quarterly, and make the current recovery point unmistakable.
I established a quarterly manual backup stored in a single ‘Most Recent Backup’ folder that overwrites the prior quarter. I also added preservation of the original launch state to the launch process.
The organization gained a recovery point beyond the host’s rolling window without creating a confusing archive of dated folders.

perspectives.name: Julie
perspectives.text: The most technically complete backup policy is useless when nobody can quickly identify or maintain it.

perspectives.name: Jae
perspectives.text: One current off-host recovery point. One preserved launch state. No folder archaeology.

perspectives.name: Min
perspectives.text: Recovery design must account for how people behave during an incident.
